content:
lina: Quick thought — we should split the policy decision surface into a fast admission path and a full-eval path. Fast path: in-memory heuristics (latency + cost) for immediate admit/reject. Full-eval: sandboxed policy runner with tenant rules and composition. I sketched a tiny RPC shape below.

omar: Strong +1 for the split. Two concerns: compatibility with existing runtime connectors, and how we version the ABI.

megan: Can we avoid a heavy sidecar? My take: small runtime shim that async-calls the policy service and falls back to a conservative local admission if the RPC times out.

raj: We ran into signal freshness issues before — probe-derived latency needs TTL semantics. If the policy uses probes, it must return a TTL for its verdict.

lina: Sketch API idea: /admit { tenant_id, hint:{latency_ms, cost_budget}, region_pref } -> { allow, variant, fallback_policy, cache_ttl_s }. Keep it intentionally minimal. Example request:
```
request {
  tenant: "acme",
  hint: { latency_ms: 50, tcost: 0.02 },
  region: "eu"
}
```

omar: Return shape looks fine. Please add `version` and `compatibility_level` fields so runtimes can opt in and degrade gracefully.

megan: Operational note — any sync RPC means p99 budget on the caller. Need client-side circuit-breaker and a local conservative fallback config baked into the runtime.

sre-oncall: Ops perspective: fast-path SLO should be 99.9% < 10ms, full-eval SLO maybe 500ms. We'll need canaries and synthetic traffic to validate.

devops-bot: deploy-note: tag changes with `policy-admit-v1` and add a feature flag so we can flip it per-tenant.

raj: Proposed plan: prototype as a sidecar exposing both v0 (legacy) and v1 endpoints over gRPC. Implement TTL semantics, a `version` header, and a light compatibility shim. Owner: raj.

lina: Follow-ups / action items: 1) raj prototype this sprint; 2) megan run benchmark to measure p99 impact on runtime; 3) omar draft compatibility/upgrade doc; 4) lina write RFC draft. Sync Tuesday @10.

omar: Question: can policy return `prefer_region: none` to indicate global fallback? If yes, should runtime then prefer cheaper region or stick to latency?

lina: Yes, policy can indicate no strong region preference. In that case the policy must also return `score_delta` and a `reason`. Runtime will only prefer alternate region if `score_delta < runtime_threshold`. Threshold will be runtime-configurable.

megan: I pushed a quick proto sketch: https://gist.github.com/xyz/policy-admit-proto (contains wire examples + headers)

raj: Noted. I'll start prototyping the sidecar and wire up a simple TTL-based cache. Thanks all.

lina: :thumbsup:
